cards.headline: Cyclone Arnab crosses Andhra coast, weakens to severe storm
cards.body: Very severe cyclonic storm Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts on the morning of October 28, 2026, before weakening into a severe cyclonic storm. The IMD said landfall was complete and the system had moved fully over land. Winds at landfall were 125-135 kmph, gusting to 150 kmph. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu said no loss of life was reported so far.
cards.why_it_matters: Cyclone preparedness and timely evacuation are central to protecting lives in India's vulnerable eastern coastal belt.
cards.key_fact: Cyclone Arnab made landfall near Narsapur, Andhra Pradesh

quiz.q: Near which town did Cyclone Arnab cross the Andhra Pradesh coast?
quiz.explain: The IMD said the cyclone crossed the coast about 20 km east-northeast of Narsapur.

cards.headline: Andhra Pradesh evacuates 89,000 as Cyclone Arnab approaches
cards.body: At least 89,000 people were evacuated from vulnerable coastal areas of Andhra Pradesh as Cyclone Arnab intensified over the Bay of Bengal ahead of landfall early on October 28. Officials said winds could reach 140 kmph. More than 2,000 cyclone shelters were set up across 20 districts, over 30,000 fishing boats secured and nearly 1,100 medical teams deployed. Neighbouring Odisha planned to evacuate around 48,000 people.
cards.why_it_matters: Mass evacuation before landfall is a key disaster-preparedness measure that helps prevent loss of life during cyclones.
cards.key_fact: Around 89,000 people evacuated in Andhra Pradesh

quiz.q: How many people did Andhra Pradesh evacuate from coastal areas ahead of Cyclone Arnab?
quiz.explain: Authorities evacuated at least 89,000 people from vulnerable coastal areas; 48,000 was the Odisha figure and 1,100 was the number of medical teams.

cards.headline: PM Modi opens science and innovation conclave at Bharat Mandapam
cards.body: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. He said India's youth are thinking big and moving forward with confidence, and urged the country to adopt future technologies and lead in building them. He cited India's development of an indigenous COVID-19 vaccine, the Mars mission and the Chandrayaan-3 landing at the lunar south pole.
cards.why_it_matters: It signals policy emphasis on home-grown technology and innovation, which shapes jobs, research funding and India's global standing.
cards.key_fact: Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave 2026

quiz.q: Where was the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave 2026 held?
quiz.explain: The Prime Minister inaugurated the conclave at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi.

cards.headline: Jaishankar to attend G20 Foreign Ministers' and Quad meetings in U.S.
cards.body: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar will travel to Atlanta in the United States from October 29 to 31, 2026, to attend the G20 Foreign Ministers' meeting hosted by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The visit will include a Quad Foreign Ministers' meeting with his Australian and Japanese counterparts. A Quad leaders' summit is planned in Manila in mid-November on the sidelines of the ASEAN-East Asian Summits.
cards.why_it_matters: G20 and Quad meetings shape cooperation on trade, maritime security and critical minerals that affect India's economy and strategic interests.
cards.key_fact: Quad leaders' summit planned in Manila in mid-November

quiz.q: Where is the Quad leaders' summit planned in mid-November?
quiz.explain: The leaders will meet in Manila on the sidelines of the ASEAN-East Asian Summits, a first in a non-Quad country.

cards.headline: Rajnath Singh calls for dismantling terrorism ecosystem at SCO
cards.body: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh told SCO member states at the 25th Council of Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, that there can be no justification for terrorism and no double standards in tackling it. He urged members to dismantle the entire terrorism ecosystem, including those who finance, support or shelter terrorists. He also sought resilient supply chains and supported a 2026-2030 trade action plan.
cards.why_it_matters: The SCO is a key platform where India raises cross-border terrorism with Pakistan and Central Asian states, shaping regional security cooperation.
cards.key_fact: 25th SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting, Dushanbe

quiz.q: Where was the 25th SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting held?
quiz.explain: Rajnath Singh spoke at the 25th SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe, Tajikistan.

cards.headline: India says UNSC reform without veto creates 'second-class' members
cards.body: India's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, told the General Assembly that any new category of permanent Security Council members without veto power would make them 'second-class' members and leave the P5 in control. He said the veto must be held by all permanent members as long as it exists, and warned that periodic elections and permanency are contradictory.
cards.why_it_matters: India has long sought a permanent UNSC seat, and its stand on the veto shapes negotiations on Council reform.
cards.key_fact: P5: China, France, Russia, UK, US hold veto power

quiz.q: How many permanent members with veto power does the UN Security Council currently have?
quiz.explain: China, France, Russia, the UK and the US are the five permanent members with veto power.

cards.headline: India to host first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi
cards.body: India will hold the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum from November 20-22 in Delhi, organised by the Culture and External Affairs Ministries. The event, proposed by PM Modi at the Tianjin summit, will be inaugurated by him at Purana Quila. Pakistan's Culture Minister Aurungzeb Khan Khichi has been invited; if he attends, it would be the first visit by a Pakistani Minister since 2023.
cards.why_it_matters: It signals limited India-Pakistan engagement through the SCO despite strained bilateral ties.
cards.key_fact: First SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, Delhi, November 20-22

quiz.q: Where will India host the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum?
quiz.explain: The event will be held at Delhi's Purana Quila, the 16th-century fort built by Emperor Humayun.

cards.headline: India's refining capacity to reach 300 million tonnes by 2030: Puri
cards.body: Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri said India's oil refining capacity will rise from about 290 million tonnes annually now to 300 million tonnes by 2030, even as Europe and other Western regions lose capacity. He said India would refine not only for itself but for the world, and could supply both domestic and export markets. He spoke at an energy meet in south Goa.
cards.why_it_matters: Refining capacity affects fuel prices, energy security and India's petroleum exports.
cards.key_fact: 300 million tonnes annual refining capacity target by 2030

quiz.q: What refining capacity does India aim to reach by 2030, according to Hardeep Singh Puri?
quiz.explain: Puri said capacity would rise from about 290 million tonnes now to 300 million tonnes by 2030.

cards.headline: RBI Governor urges states to adopt prudent borrowing and better spending
cards.body: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra asked state governments to improve expenditure quality, strengthen cash management and borrow prudently for long-term fiscal sustainability. Speaking at the 36th Conference of State Finance Secretaries in Mumbai, he urged states to onboard the Unified Lending Interface and use programmable central bank digital currency for direct benefit transfers. He also released a compendium on cash and debt management for states.
cards.why_it_matters: State borrowing and spending affect public debt, interest costs and the delivery of welfare schemes to citizens.
cards.key_fact: Unified Lending Interface (ULI) for easier credit flow

quiz.q: Which platform did the RBI Governor urge states to onboard?
quiz.explain: Malhotra urged states to onboard the Unified Lending Interface (ULI) and use P-CBDC for DBT.

cards.headline: Raghuram Rajan advises India not to defend rupee at any cost
cards.body: Former RBI governor Raghuram Rajan said India should not panic over the rupee's slide or fixate on a particular exchange rate, Reuters reported. The rupee has fallen around 6% in 2026 and hit a record low of 96.96 in May, pressured by costly crude, higher US Treasury yields and foreign outflows. Rajan cautioned that defending the currency aggressively could drain foreign exchange reserves and that a wider current account deficit remains a risk if oil stays high.
cards.why_it_matters: Exchange-rate policy affects import costs, inflation and foreign reserves, so how the RBI handles the rupee's fall touches ordinary households through prices.
cards.key_fact: Rupee fell about 6% in 2026; record low 96.96 in May

quiz.q: According to the report, what record low did the rupee touch in May?
quiz.explain: The article states the rupee touched a record low of 96.96 in May.

cards.headline: New GST rules on post-sale discounts, export refunds from 1 November
cards.body: The finance ministry notified 1 November as the date for GST rule changes covering post-sale discounts, export refunds and procedures, bringing Sections 153-155 of the Finance Act, 2026 into force. Businesses can now exclude eligible post-supply discounts from taxable value via credit notes if recipients reverse input tax credit, without the earlier requirement of a prior agreement. CBIC also issued six circulars clarifying Rule 96(10)'s retrospective omission after a Supreme Court ruling.
cards.why_it_matters: Clearer discount and refund rules reduce compliance costs and disputes for businesses, which can affect prices and ease of doing business.
cards.key_fact: Finance Act 2026 Sections 153-155; CGST Act 2017 amended

quiz.q: Which Act's sections does the notification bring into force on 1 November?
quiz.explain: The finance ministry notified Sections 153 to 155 of the Finance Act, 2026.

cards.headline: Jio Platforms lists at 21% premium after record $3.2 billion IPO
cards.body: Jio Platforms shares opened at 1,358 rupees on debut, a 21% premium over the 1,119-rupee offer price, after India's biggest-ever IPO of about $3.2 billion. The listing gives Reliance Industries its first listing in two decades and makes Jio one of India's largest companies by market capitalisation. Jio's telecom business serves over 530 million customers, and the company is backed by Meta and Google.
cards.why_it_matters: The listing signals deepening Indian capital markets and gives retail investors a large new telecom-and-digital stock to track.

quiz.q: At what price did Jio Platforms shares open on debut?
quiz.explain: The stock opened at 1,358 rupees against an offer price of 1,119 rupees.

cards.headline: Industrial credit growth nears 20%, hints at private capex revival
cards.body: Shaktikanta Das, principal secretary to the Prime Minister and former RBI governor, said bank credit to industry grew nearly 20% in July, an early sign of private investment revival after corporate balance-sheet repair following the pandemic. Speaking at a BFSI summit, he urged banks to finance infrastructure, semiconductors, electronics and defence, and called for closer monitoring of household consumption debt and a larger role for municipal bond markets.
cards.why_it_matters: Private investment drives jobs and growth; stronger industrial credit can translate into more capacity and employment over time.
cards.key_fact: Bank credit to industry grew nearly 20% in July

quiz.q: By how much did bank credit to industry grow in July, per Das?
quiz.explain: Das said bank credit to industry grew nearly 20% in July.

cards.headline: Supreme Court seeks Centre's reply on Vande Mataram pleas
cards.body: The Supreme Court sought the Union government's response to two petitions challenging orders imposing the six-stanza Vande Mataram. Petitioners B.D. Borkar and former IAS officer Balakrishnan Sathyabhama Mavoji called it a divisive religious war song and said the January 28 and July 9 orders violate fundamental rights. They argued the two-stanza non-theistic version used since independence was peaceful, while the six-stanza Anandamath version promotes sectarian division.
cards.why_it_matters: The case tests the balance between state-promoted symbols and the fundamental rights of religious minorities.
cards.key_fact: Six-stanza Vande Mataram from Bankim Chandra's Anandamath

quiz.q: Which novel contains the six-stanza Vande Mataram?
quiz.explain: The six-stanza version was introduced by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee in his novel Anandamath.

cards.headline: Madras HC: Non-Hindus with religious markers barred from Agamic temples
cards.body: The Madras High Court heard a PIL by K. Thangam Venkatesh seeking enforcement of the Tamil Nadu Temple Entry Authorisation Act. A Division Bench of Justices G.R. Swaminathan and P. Murugan said non-Hindus must not cross beyond the flag pole in Agamic temples, as this would defile temple sanctity. The court cited instances of breaches and confined its ruling to Agamic temples.
cards.why_it_matters: It clarifies how temple-entry law applies to a specific class of temples, balancing religious custom with statutory rules that ordinary worshippers encounter at the temple gate.
cards.key_fact: Tamil Nadu Temple Entry Authorisation Act regulates temple entry

quiz.q: Which law did the petitioner seek to enforce in this case?
options: Tamil Nadu Temple Entry Authorisation Act
quiz.explain: The PIL sought strict enforcement of the Tamil Nadu Temple Entry Authorisation Act and its Rules.

cards.headline: Former SC judge Oka calls for transparent Supreme Court roster
cards.body: Former Supreme Court judge Abhay S. Oka said the Supreme Court's roster needs an overhaul so that case allocation is transparent and free of manual intervention. Speaking at a CJAR event on judicial accountability in New Delhi, he noted that several Benches handle the same case categories, leaving litigants unsure which Bench will hear a fresh case. He called the court too Chief Justice-centric.
cards.why_it_matters: A clearer roster affects which judges hear a case, a basic element of fair and predictable justice for any litigant.
cards.key_fact: CJI is the master of the roster

quiz.q: Who is described as the 'master of the roster' with authority to constitute Benches?
quiz.explain: The article states the CJI, as master of the roster, has administrative authority to constitute Benches and allocate work.

cards.headline: Digital news publishers challenge DPDP Act in Supreme Court
cards.body: The Digital News Publishers Association challenged provisions of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the 2025 Rules, arguing they violate journalistic freedom. A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant is to hear the petitions. The DNPA said the law imposes notice and consent rules without an exemption for journalism and cites Section 36's broad information powers.
cards.why_it_matters: Data protection rules can affect how reporters gather and protect information, which bears on the public's right to know.

quiz.q: Which law has the DNPA challenged before the Supreme Court?
options: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act
quiz.explain: The DNPA challenged provisions of the DPDP Act, 2023 and the DPDP Rules, 2025.

cards.headline: Karnataka publishes final electoral roll after SIR
cards.body: Karnataka's final electoral roll under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) has been published, with constituency-wise lists on the Chief Electoral Officer's website. Over 99.32 lakh names were removed during the exercise. Officials said the SIR aimed to ensure every eligible voter was included and ineligible names removed, to achieve a clean electorate.
cards.why_it_matters: Electoral rolls decide who can vote, so large-scale deletions matter to every voter in the state.
cards.key_fact: Over 99.32 lakh names removed in Karnataka SIR

quiz.q: How many names were removed from Karnataka's rolls in the SIR?
quiz.explain: The article says more than 99.32 lakh names were knocked off the rolls in Karnataka.

cards.headline: Semiconductor Summit 2026 held in Chennai
cards.body: SRM Institute of Science and Technology, in association with The Hindu Group, organised the Semiconductor Summit 2026 in Chennai on October 27, 2026. It brought together innovators, engineers and industry leaders to discuss chip design, power efficiency and next-generation materials. Speakers included Kamaljeet Singh, Director General of the Semi-Conductor Laboratory, Mohali, under MeitY.
cards.why_it_matters: Semiconductors power everyday electronics, and such discussions track India's push to build its own chip industry.

quiz.q: Which institution organised the Semiconductor Summit 2026 along with The Hindu Group?
options: SRM Institute of Science and Technology
quiz.explain: SRMIST organised the summit in association with The Hindu Group in Chennai.
